asDecan.p: Your Sun sits somewhere between 20 and 29 degrees of Taurus, the last of the sign's three ten-degree slices, or decans. In the Chaldean order Saturn rules this one. Saturn has no special dignity in Taurus, which means it isn't strengthened or weakened there. It's a visitor, and it picks up the manners of the house, which here means Venus, the sign's ruler. So you've got the planet of time and limits living in the sign of comfort and good food, an odd mix when you think about it. The Five of Pentacles, Mercury's slice, opens Taurus worried about being left out in the cold, and the Six, the Moon's slice, is busy giving and receiving. By the Seven the sign is ripe and already leaning toward Gemini. Have a look at the man in the picture, leaning on his hoe and staring at the vine. He's put the work down and he's counting. The Hierophant is still your Sun card, and the Seven fills in the detail.

You're the one at a family dinner who asks your cousin how the business is actually going, and then wants the numbers. You check a savings balance the way other people check the weather. When a friend sends a photo of their new sourdough starter, part of you is already wondering whether it'll still be alive by March. A Sunday with nothing planned tends to end up in the garden or at the kitchen bench, doing something with your hands that leaves a result you can look at on Monday. Venus gives you a real taste for good things, a decent coat, a proper chair. Saturn wants to know what they'll be like in ten years before you pay for them. So you'll stand in a shop for twenty minutes over one jumper, go home without it, come back for it on Saturday, and then wear it until the elbows go.

Everyone knows you can wait. What's less obvious is that Saturn in these degrees gives you a sharp eye for what isn't growing, and the nerve to say so out loud. A friend has been pouring money into a café for three years, and you're the one who can sit down with them over the books and say, kindly, that it's the lease that's sinking it. They'll hear it from you, because they know you'd have been the first to tell them if it was working. At work you're good at the review nobody else wants to do, the one where somebody actually looks at what a project cost and what it gave back. You don't make a drama of it, and you usually offer to help with whatever comes next.

You keep a private ledger, and you'd probably deny it. You know who drove to the airport last time, whose turn it is to host Christmas, how many years you've carried a particular friendship without much coming back. Saturn measures things wherever it lands, and in a sign ruled by Venus the thing it ends up measuring is affection, which is a bit of a problem. Most of the time the ledger stays in the drawer. Then your sister cancels for the third time and the whole account comes out in one evening, going back to 2009, and she has no idea where any of it came from. There's a quieter version as well. You're slow to start anything whose payoff you can't picture, so the evening class, the odd little side project, the trip with no plan, mostly don't happen.

When something goes wrong, a redundancy, bad news about a parent's health, a relationship ending after years, your first move is to go very still. You eat the same meals, keep the same hours, water the plants, and look almost unbothered to anyone watching. Taurus is good at holding steady under fire. A week or so later the stillness has gone heavy. You're going back over every year you put into the thing that failed and adding up what it cost, and Saturn is very thorough with that sort of arithmetic. Messages go unanswered without you quite deciding to ignore them. The people close to you find this hard, because you look fine and you won't be hurried. What helps is a physical job with a result you can see by evening, painting a fence, cooking for a crowd, digging out a tired garden bed. After a day or two of that you're usually ready to talk.

You're fairly old-fashioned in love, which is the Taurus in you, and this slice adds Saturn's habit of stopping to check how things are going. It tends to surprise partners. Every so often, usually around an anniversary or a birthday, you want to talk about the relationship itself, what's working, what's gone stale, whether the plan for the house still makes sense. To you that's care. To someone who doesn't know you well it can feel like a performance review, and I've seen partners of late-Taurus Suns go pale at the words 'can we have a chat'. Venus gives you plenty of warmth and a real appetite for touch, good food and slow evenings in, and you show love by keeping things running, the car serviced, the good sheets washed and back on the bed. You do best with someone who answers the check-in honestly.

Work that pays off late suits you. Vineyards and orchards, obviously, but also funds management, building up a physio practice over fifteen years, restoring old furniture, teaching the same subject until you're the person everyone rings. You know the three-year numbers by heart while everyone else is talking about this quarter. Saturn gives you the stamina for the dull middle of a project, the stretch other people drift away from. What tends to go wrong is the end. You grow the account, the client list, the team, and then somebody better at talking in meetings takes the credit, and you let it go because making a fuss feels cheap. When the results come in, ask for your share of them in writing.

At twenty this decan can feel stuck, to be honest. Friends are moving cities, changing courses, trying things, and you're still in the same part-time job because you want to see where it goes, and you worry you're behind. By the mid-thirties the picture tends to flip. Things you started quietly ten years earlier, a savings habit, a skill, a friendship, a small business, have grown into something solid, and people start asking how you did it. That's usually also when the private ledger costs you something, a friend lost over an old account nobody else remembered. These are the last degrees before Gemini, and the fifties often let a bit of Gemini in. People with this decan get curious again, take up an instrument, go back to study for no return at all, and seem to enjoy it.

Plant a tomato or a chilli from seed, in a pot by the back door, and keep a scrap of paper under it. Each time you water it, write down one thing in your life you're waiting on, and under that, one honest line about whether it's moving. Don't decide anything yet. When the plant fruits, or dies, read the whole list back. Anything that's on there five times with no change in the second line either gets crossed off or gets a phone call.
